title: Private Deploy: Rollback & Migration Contract for Air-Gapped and Limited-Egress VPCs
creator: Priya Raman
description: PRD / acceptance contract that formalizes rollback and migration behavior for Private/VPC deployments operating under strict egress constraints (air-gapped, limited egress windows, outbound allowlist). Focus is on operator-driven upgrades, safe rollback paths, artifact provenance checks, and deterministic acceptance tests that customers can run during maintenance windows.
problem_statement: Customers running Private/VPC deployments with restricted network egress need predictable, auditable upgrade and rollback behavior that does not rely on continuous internet access. Current upgrade documentation is fragmented; customers report uncertainty about safe rollback scenarios, image provenance validation in offline contexts, and operator lifecycle actions when a canary fails under limited egress conditions.
goals: 1) Define deterministic upgrade and rollback contracts that work for air-gapped or allowlisted environments. 2) Provide operational acceptance criteria and test artifacts customers can use during maintenance windows. 3) Ensure artifact provenance and signature verification functions with staged mirrors or physical media fallback. 4) Minimize customer blast radius by constraining automated actions and exposing clear operator steps.
success_metrics: - Reduce on-call upgrade-related incidents for Private customers by 60% in the three months after release. - Customer verification playbook executed successfully by at least three beta sites. - Documented rollback path validated in automated canary simulations and post-mortem shows <10% data-loss-related incidents.
non_goals: - This work does not change hosted API upgrade flows. - We will not build a bespoke airgap artifact distribution network; we will define compatibility for existing mirror and physical-media workflows. - Not adding automated cross-region replication for customer data in this scope.
scope_changes: - Initial scope included automated operator rollback hooks; revised to require explicit operator approval for rollback in air-gapped contexts. - Added a small compatibility shim to support detached KMS rotation during migration after customer feedback.
technical_requirements: Operator must be able to trigger a safe rollback from the control plane or CLI without outbound connectivity to Redwood's central services.
Upgrade images and operator manifests must be cryptographically signed; signature verification must succeed against locally-stored public keys or mirrored key bundles.
Support staged artifact validation: image checksum, signature, and release metadata must be verifiable from a local mirror or supplied tarball/USB media.
Upgrade process must include a pre-flight dry-run mode producing a deterministic report (checksums, resource diffs, estimated downtime).
Rollback must preserve customer-configured secrets (KMS/HSM keys) unless operator explicitly requests a key rotation workflow.
All on-node operators should support a read-only 'verify-only' mode for customers to confirm artifacts before committing changes.
network_requirements: Minimum: ability to fetch artifacts from a customer-controlled mirror or accept operator-provided tarball via on-prem mirror.
Egress window mode: system may fetch limited metadata (hash lists) during scheduled allowlist windows; full artifact download should be deferred to mirror.
Split-horizon DNS support: operator can resolve internal registries differently during upgrades to point to mirrors.
No persistent dependency on Redwood-hosted endpoints during the upgrade pipeline for air-gapped installs.
upgrade_requirements: Canary sequencing: single-node canary, partial-node canary (subset of replicas), and full rollout stages documented and scriptable.
Explicit operator checkpoints between stages requiring manual approve/continue in air-gapped mode.
Pre- and post-upgrade health probes must be run locally and produce machine-readable reports storable to the cluster for later audit.
Graceful KDumps: ensure long-running requests are drained or preserved based on customer rollback policy.
airgap_constraints: Artifact transfer via removable media must include manifest.json, sha256sum, and detached signature (RFC 4880 or similar).
Operator checklist for physical media: integrity verification, operator identity verification, and local key acceptance steps.
No change to KMS/HSM trust anchors without explicit operator confirmation and recorded audit event.
Support a 'simulated-offline' test mode that runs the upgrade using mirrored artifacts in a sandbox without committing changes to production.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Given a Private deployment with zero egress, a resident operator can perform a full upgrade using a supplied tarball and pass signature + checksum validation without contacting Redwood-hosted services.

AC-2: Canary failure during an air-gapped upgrade triggers a documented operator rollback procedure; executing the procedure returns the cluster to previous version within defined SLO (configurable per-customer, default 30 minutes), with clear logged audit trail.
AC-3: Pre-flight dry-run outputs deterministic report; sample reports included in artifacts and accepted by customer QA in beta sites.
AC-4: Image provenance verification succeeds when public key is supplied via mirror bundle; mismatch halts upgrade and surfaces clear remediation steps.
AC-5: Upgrade CLI/Console exposes 'verify-only' and 'approve-and-apply' flows; in air-gapped mode 'approve-and-apply' requires a unique operator token generated and recorded locally.
rollout_plan: Beta with 3 customer sites over 6 weeks: Week 1 internal staging and simulated-offline tests; Week 2–3 two pilot customers (one fully air-gapped, one limited-egress); Week 4 incorporate feedback; Week 5–6 third pilot + documentation freeze. Rollout disabled for customers without signed acceptance of operator checklist.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Local health reports captured and exportable as artifacts for post-upgrade audit.

Operator actions must populate local audit log with timestamps, operator identity, and signature of the action. These logs are downloadable and verifiable by Redwood support when permitted by customer.
Telemetry from limited-egress upgrades should be optionally queued and sent during next allowed egress window if the customer opts in.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Operator mis-applies rollback in partially-upgraded clusters -> Mitigation: add a dry-run and cluster-state validator that blocks irreversible actions until operator confirms.
Risk: Corrupt physical media -> Mitigation: require at least two matching artifact sources (mirror + media) or cryptographic signature pass.
Risk: KMS mismatch during rollback -> Mitigation: detect key rotation and surface 'manual reconcile' playbook with minimal downtime.
open_questions: Q1: Do we require Redwood-signed operator tokens for 'approve-and-apply' in fully air-gapped installations, or is locally-generated operator token sufficient?
Q2: What is the canonical format for detached signatures in our airgap playbook (OpenPGP vs CMS)?
Q3: Should we support a fallback that copies operator-approved artifacts into an immutable local registry automatically?
